title: Kinematics of Motion in a Straight Line Module 2 Lesson 1: Connected Free Flight Motion custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Two particles $A$ and $B$ are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. The system is released from rest with particle $B$ at a height of $2.25\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. While both particles are in motion, the acceleration of the system is $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find the speed of particle $A$ at the instant particle $B$ strikes the ground.

Particle $A$ is moving vertically upwards with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at the instant the string connected to it becomes slack. Particle $A$ then moves freely under gravity without reaching the pulley. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the additional distance that $A$ rises before coming to instantaneous rest.

At the instant particle $B$ hits the ground, particle $A$ is moving vertically upwards with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Particle $A$ then moves freely under gravity without reaching the pulley. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the time taken for particle $A$ to reach its highest point after $B$ strikes the ground.

A particle $A$ on a rough horizontal table is connected by a string passing over a smooth pulley to a hanging particle $B$. At the instant $B$ hits the ground, $A$ is moving with speed $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Once the string is slack, friction causes $A$ to decelerate at $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find the distance that $A$ travels after $B$ hits the ground before coming to rest.

Two particles $A$ and $B$ are initially held at rest at a height of $1.5\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground, connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley. When the system is released, $B$ descends and hits the ground. At the instant of impact, $A$ has speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the maximum height reached by $A$ above the ground.

A particle reaches a maximum height of $4.05\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground while the connecting string is slack. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the time taken for the particle to fall from this maximum height to the ground.

questions.prompt: Two particles $A$ and $B$, of masses $3\text{ kg}$ and $5\text{ kg}$ respectively, are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a fixed smooth pulley. Both particles are initially held at rest at a height of $1.8\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. The system is released from rest. Particle $B$ moves downwards and hits the ground without rebounding. The string becomes slack and particle $A$ does not reach the pulley in its subsequent motion. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the acceleration of the system while the string is taut is $2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and find the speed of $A$ and the time taken at the instant $B$ hits the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum height reached by $A$ above the ground, and find the total time from release until $A$ reaches this maximum height.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ rests on a smooth horizontal table. It is connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to a particle $B$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ hanging freely. Particle $B$ is initially $0.5\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground, and particle $A$ is $2.0\text{ m}$ from the pulley. The system is released from rest. Particle $B$ strikes the ground and remains at rest. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of the system while $B$ is descending, and calculate the speed of $A$ at the instant $B$ hits the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: After $B$ hits the ground, $A$ moves across a rough section of the table which exerts a constant deceleration of $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find the distance $A$ travels while decelerating, and determine whether $A$ reaches the pulley.

questions.prompt: Two particles $P$ and $Q$, of masses $0.3\text{ kg}$ and $0.5\text{ kg}$ respectively, are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a fixed smooth pulley. The particles are initially held at rest at the same level, $0.8\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. At time $t = 0$, the system is released. When $Q$ strikes the ground, it remains at rest and the string becomes slack. Particle $P$ does not reach the pulley in its subsequent motion. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $P$ and the time elapsed when $Q$ strikes the ground, and calculate the maximum height reached by $P$ above the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: After reaching its maximum height, $P$ falls vertically downwards to the ground. Find the speed with which $P$ strikes the ground, and the total time elapsed from $t = 0$ until $P$ hits the ground.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is on a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. A light inextensible string attached to $A$ passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline and supports a hanging particle $B$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$. The system is released from rest with $B$ at a height of $2.0\text{ m}$ above the floor. Particle $B$ strikes the floor and does not rebound. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of the system while $B$ is descending, and calculate the speed of $A$ at the instant $B$ hits the floor.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: When $B$ hits the floor, the string becomes slack and $A$ continues to move up the smooth incline freely under gravity. Find the additional distance $A$ moves up the incline before coming to instantaneous rest, and the total time from release until $A$ comes to rest.

questions.prompt: A connected system starts from rest at $t = 0$ and accelerates uniformly at $2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $2\text{ s}$ until the descending particle strikes the ground. The ascending particle $A$ then moves vertically upwards freely under gravity until coming to instantaneous rest at its highest point. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of particle $A$ at the instant the descending particle strikes the ground, the time taken for $A$ to reach its maximum height from this instant, and the total height gained by $A$ from its initial position.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State the coordinates $(t, v)$ of the three key vertices on the velocity-time graph for particle $A$ from release until it comes to rest at its highest point, and verify the total distance by calculating the area under the graph.

questions.prompt: Two particles $A$ and $B$, of masses $0.3\text{ kg}$ and $0.5\text{ kg}$ respectively, are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string passing over a fixed smooth pulley. Both particles are initially held at rest at a height of $0.8\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. At time $t = 0$, the system is released. When particle $B$ strikes the ground, it remains at rest and the string becomes slack. Particle $A$ continues to move vertically upwards, does not reach the pulley, and subsequently falls to the ground. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the tension in the string and the acceleration of the system while the string is taut, and determine the speed of $A$ and the elapsed time when $B$ strikes the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum height reached by $A$ above the ground, the speed with which $A$ strikes the ground, and the total time elapsed from $t = 0$ until $A$ hits the ground.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. It is connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging particle $B$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$. A constant frictional resistance of $1.0\text{ N}$ opposes the motion of $A$ along the plane. The system is released from rest with $B$ at a height of $1.5\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. When $B$ hits the ground, it remains at rest. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of the system while $B$ is descending, the tension in the string, and the speed of $A$ at the instant $B$ hits the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the deceleration of $A$ after the string becomes slack, calculate the additional distance $A$ moves up the slope before coming to instantaneous rest, and find the total time from release until $A$ comes to rest.
